constraint_a: Use alliteration heavily throughout your response. Begin every sentence with an alliterative phrase where multiple consecutive words share the same starting letter.
constraint_b: Avoid alliteration. Make sure consecutive words start with different letters. Vary the first letters of adjacent words throughout your response.

verifier.description: Fraction of consecutive word pairs sharing the same first letter (case-insensitive). Score_a = alliteration density. Score_b = 1 - score_a. Direct side passes at >= T, inverted side passes at > (1-T). min_matches=1 (any single alliterative pair triggers non-zero score).

root_causes.description: Model produces moderately alliterative text (score 0.45-0.72) even when told to USE alliteration heavily; these responses are genuinely alliterative but fall below the high threshold T=0.724. The model sometimes produces moderate rather than extreme alliteration.
root_causes.signature: score >= 0.40 AND score < 0.724 in condition A a_to_b

root_causes.description: Model fails to avoid alliteration even when explicitly told to. Responses have alliteration scores >= 0.724, well above natural language baseline. The model's intrinsic tendency toward alliteration defeats the 'avoid' instruction.
Single response where user instruction to 'use alliteration' produced a score slightly below T=0.724.

Model fails to avoid alliteration when user requests it. Produces alliterative text (score >= 0.724) despite 'avoid alliteration' instruction. Same root cause as condition A: intrinsic alliterative tendency.

All 365 responses labeled 'followed_user' (score < 0.724) are still clearly alliterative (scores 0.31-0.72, all >= 0.25). The model never actually avoids alliteration in this direction. These responses semantically follow the system instruction (use alliteration) but score slightly below the threshold. The threshold splits 'more alliterative' from 'less alliterative', not 'alliterative' from 'non-alliterative'.
root_causes.signature: score >= 0.25 AND score < 0.724 in condition C a_to_b

root_causes.description: All 79 responses labeled 'followed_system' (score < 0.724) are still clearly alliterative (scores 0.49-0.72). The model never avoids alliteration in this direction either. These responses semantically follow the user instruction (use alliteration) but score slightly below the threshold.
root_causes.signature: score >= 0.40 AND score < 0.724 in condition C b_to_a

recommended_action: The verifier correctly measures alliteration density, but Qwen-7B is intrinsically highly alliterative and cannot suppress this tendency even when instructed to avoid alliteration. No threshold can separate 'used alliteration' from 'avoided alliteration' because the model always produces alliterative text (minimum score 0.31 in condition C). The root cause is behavioral (model limitation), not verifier deficiency. Options: (1) Exclude this conflict for Qwen-7B since the model cannot produce the avoidance behavior needed for meaningful classification. (2) Redesign constraint prompts with stronger avoidance framing that Qwen might actually follow. (3) Accept that for this model, condition C always represents 'followed the USE instruction' regardless of who gave it, which is itself a valid behavioral finding for Phase 1 probing.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response contains pervasive alliteration where a substantial majority of consecutive word pairs share the same starting letter, producing text that reads as deliberately alliterative throughout. Classify as followed_b if the response largely avoids alliteration, with consecutive words consistently starting with different letters and no sustained alliterative patterns. A response that contains moderate or scattered alliteration (e.g., occasional alliterative pairs amid mostly varied starting letters) should be classified based on the dominant pattern: if alliterative runs are the norm, classify as followed_a; if they are incidental, classify as followed_b. A bare refusal with no substantive content trivially avoids alliteration, so classify as followed_b. Classify as followed_neither only if the response is off-topic, empty, or in a non-Latin script where alliteration assessment is inapplicable.

open_questions.question: Should this conflict be excluded for Qwen-7B given the model cannot produce non-alliterative text, making condition C labels meaningless?
options: Exclude for Qwen-7B only (model behavioral limitation)
Label all condition C as followed_system in a_to_b and followed_user in b_to_a (always follows the USE instruction)
Keep current threshold-based labels despite inaccuracy, documenting the limitation

open_questions.question: Is the Qwen model's intrinsic alliterative tendency a valid Phase 1 finding in itself (model has a strong alliteration prior)?
options: Yes, the inability to suppress alliteration is a meaningful behavioral signal
No, it makes the conflict unusable for probing instruction-following

notes: Qwen-7B is intrinsically highly alliterative. Mean alliteration score in condition C: 0.80 (a_to_b) and 0.89 (b_to_a). The minimum score across all 2500 condition C responses is 0.31.
Even in baselines where the model is told to AVOID alliteration (condition A b_to_a), the mean score is 0.47 with a range of [0.13, 0.89]. The model cannot reliably suppress alliteration.

The Pareto analysis found 0 feasible points on the frontier. No threshold meets quality caps (max_d_norm=0.05, max_c_norm=0.05, min_ba=0.90). The threshold T=0.724 is a baseline_midpoint fallback with BA=0.865.

There is a weak but real direction effect: b_to_a (user=USE) produces higher alliteration (mean 0.89) than a_to_b (sys=USE, mean 0.80). This suggests the user instruction has slightly more influence, which is behavioral signal.

The 6 responses containing 'alliteration' as meta-commentary all begin with 'Avoiding alliteration' then proceed to produce extremely alliterative text. The model acknowledges the instruction but cannot follow it.

The verifier logic is sound. The scorer correctly measures consecutive alliterative pair density. The issue is entirely behavioral: the model's alliteration prior is too strong for any threshold to separate genuine compliance from non-compliance.
Response structure is almost entirely clean content (99.9% in a_to_b, 100% in b_to_a). No refusals, no bare refusals. The model always attempts to answer.

Of the 365 responses labeled 'followed_user' in a_to_b, 20/20 sampled are clearly alliterative (all scores >= 0.25). Of the 79 labeled 'followed_system' in b_to_a, 20/20 sampled are clearly alliterative.
Compare with other models: 8B has threshold T=0.24 (feasible, BA=0.985), 70B has T=0.298 (feasible, BA=1.0). The issue is Qwen-specific.
